- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overestimating recovery.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by steep decline, reduce peak by 5–10% to account for overshoot.
- If recent 3–5 day mean is trending upward, forecast should not lag more than 2–3 days; if lagged, adjust forward by 1–2 points.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), forecast should align with 18-day moving average, not 30-day trend.
- If forecast consistently overestimates true outcome by >3% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to correct for mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast by 1–2% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
